mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and new home sales (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer and housing demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the 10-year Treasury yield (implied by RSAFS and FEDFUNDS dynamics) below 3.5% combined with rising CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3%) signals a flattening yield curve and inflation uncertainty, which increases volatility and reduces equity valuations over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% and FEDFUNDS < 3.5% and RSAFS trend negative for one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 in a single month, accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate, signals a tight labor market that boosts wage inflation and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly increase in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based supply recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average and HOUST > 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
